recipes.name: Fennel Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 medium orange, peeled and broken into sections

steps.text: Make dressing: Whisk sugar, vinegar, oil, basil, salt, and pepper together in a small bowl until sugar dissolves.
Make salad: Toss salad greens, orange sections, fennel, onion, almonds, and cranberries together in a large serving bowl until evenly combined.
Pour dressing over salad and toss to combine.

raw_recipe.headline: Fennel Salad
raw_recipe.description: This fennel salad combines thinly sliced fennel with crisp greens, orange, cranberries, crunchy almonds, and a tangy vinaigrette for an elegant side.

review.reviewBody: I made this salad especially for my husband - I am not a huge fan of fennel or raw onion, but he is. He is rating it 5 stars - yes, he understands the system. :) In my hurry to get through the grocery store, I accidentally grabbed dried cherries instead of cranberries - so I used them and they worked fine with this (although quite a bit more expensive I noticed later, so feel free to stick with cranberries). Thanks for the recipe - he would like to have it again soon! :)

This salad is refreshing, crunchy, and a nice change. I doubled the recipe and used spring mix and arugula. I toasted the almonds. The dressing - I followed the amounts but used citrus habanero olive oil and lime olive oil, and lemon infused balsamic vinegar and pineapple infused olive oil...that took the place of the sugar. I also used the red vinegar called for in the recipe. I took this to Friendsgiving and it was a hit.

I loved it, my family loved it, my friends loved it. I add pomelo sections with the orange.... Using a mandoline slicer for the fennel and the onions makes the job very easy. I use fresh Arugula/Rocca/Watercress from my garden.
Making without sugar (using Keto friendly monkfruit sweetener) and chopped walnuts instead of almonds. Reduces carbs drsmatically!

I altered it a bit… I didn’t add any extra salad greens, only fennel. I substituted pine nuts for almonds slivers. I substituted pomegranate seeds for cranberries. I substituted a tangerine for an orange. My family LOVED it. Ate every last bit of it and asked for more. The dressing is delicious. I’ll say, the substitutions have it a fresher taste. I cut up and added a bit of the top of the fennel as well just for presentation and it was stunning. 10/10

This was very good - made it to bring to Easter dinner and everyone loved it. I used a bag of spring greens plus a fair amount of romaine for a large bowl and used two oranges instead of one. I also added a little orange zest to the dressing. Even with this very large salad the amount of dressing the recipe made was way more than I needed.

This is one of my favorite salads! Because I cook for one, I chose to use a combination of romaine and iceberg lettuces that I had in my fridge. Again, using what I had on hand, I substituted sliced almonds for slivered and one time with chopped pistachios. All good!

Glad I found this recipe! Always wanted to try an orange/fennel salad and this was good. I read some reviews and did a combo as I didn't have all ingredients on hand, and did not want a lot of sugar in the dressing. Used cherries instead of cranberries, stevia and a little fig balsamic in addition to the red wine vinegar in the dressing, and added some dried basil to that (just a pinch) as I did not have fresh. Very colorful and tasty. Will be making this again and using the fresh basil. Yum!

Made this up for 2 of us. Pared down the sugar and didn't have fresh basil on hand. But made it enough in advance that the dried basil worked fine. We loved this salad. It went perfectly with the Sausage, Fennel, Penne, Pecorino dish I made. Just held back a bit of the fennel bulb for the salad. Yummy, yummy, yummy

I made half this recipe for Easter Dinner and it was loved! I used two small blood oranges but otherwise followed recipe in reduced amounts in accordance for a 5 oz clamshell of mixed greens! Thank you! Delightful!
The flavors were great but too sweet so I cut the sugar in half and it helped. I have made it twice and cutting the sugar made it very good

This salad is so delicious! It’s a fan favorite for all ages. For us, it makes twice as much dressing as we use for the recipe of salad makings so I either double the other ingredients or halve the dressing.
This salad is great for brining to a party. We used about 1/2 to 2/3 of the dressing and it was perfect. Anything more would be too much
The flavours/combinations of, surpised me; it was delicious. I will definitely try it again.

This was delicious! I had never used fennel before but i bought some at the farmers market I wanted to try. I made exactly as directed but i added some cucumber i wanted to use up and i had dried cherries rather than cranberries.

I made this as directed and it was a hit at Easter dinner. I did not have experience with fennel so I checked out a couple of you tube videos about how to clean and chop fennel. I will definitely make this again.
